$comment: Pinned PUC Lua `luac` binaries for the MAINT-35 parse oracle, one per LuaLanguageLevel: one
TOOLING-09 linux-x86_64 release archive (internetisalie/lua-binaries) per level.
fetch-luac.py downloads each archive, REFUSES on a sha256 mismatch, and caches
test/luac/<version>/luac. ParseOracle resolves exactly that path and never consults PATH.
Why not a distro package: apt gives whatever the release carries (Debian ships 5.1.5-11,
5.4.8-x — patched, and floating with the distro). MAINT-33 pins every corpus checkout to a
commit SHA so the sweep is reproducible; pinning the corpus while letting the JUDGE drift is
incoherent. Worse, a PATH search lets two machines judge by different binaries while the gate
The digests are the release's own SHA256SUMS, so trust rests on the TOOLING-09 build
repository: the digest pins our artefact, it does not vouch for lua.org's source.
Policy: pin the release TOOLING-09 publishes for each minor version.
LUA50 is deliberately absent — PUC 5.0 is not a supported target, and requireBinary throws.
